A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SCULPT, with matching authors, core methodology and retained experiments. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-4o and Llama-3.1 experiments, aggregation ablations, prompt-perturbation tests and action-distribution analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds multi-label evaluations, experiments with LAPE-generated initial prompts, prompt-comparison measurements and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The core critic-actor updates, aggregation alternatives, actions and UCB search remain. v2 Section 3.1 and Appendix N introduce GPT-4o-based structuring of unformatted prompts, whereas v1 Section 7 lists automated structuring as future work. LAPE initialization also becomes an implemented optional pipeline. Renaming the reflection and aggregation components does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds GoEmotions, classifying Reddit comments into 28 emotion categories, and BeaverTails, assigning QA responses to multiple categories across 14 harm types. These introduce multi-label requirements beyond the retained four BBH and four RAI tasks. It also evaluates LAPE-generated starting prompts as an additional input scenario.

E2.justification: The GPT-4o comparison gains the LAPE-initialized SCULPT variant. External baselines remain APE, Long-APE/LAPE, APEX, OPRO and ProTeGi; Long-APE is renamed rather than replaced. Initial Prompt already participated in v1's tables despite being newly enumerated in v2's baseline description.

E3.justification: Added protocols include LAPE initialization, chunked Sentence Transformer similarity, GPT-4o scoring of preservation and dissimilarity, and token/cost accounting. The new multi-label evaluations use accuracy, 1,000 training and 1,000 test examples each, with 1,020 BeaverTails and 3,426 GoEmotions validation examples. Existing task splits, model temperatures and search budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an initialization study testing dependence on expert prompts, a three-metric analysis of information preservation and prompt changes, and a computational comparison with ProTeGi. Existing aggregation ablations, perturbation tests, optimization-step curves, action distributions and worked refinement examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions average the top four prompts across three trials and report uncertainty alongside benchmark scores. v2 relocates GPT-4o standard deviations into Appendix A, Tables 7–9. It introduces no new seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice; changes to individual deviation values belong to E6.

E6.justification: v2 adds multi-label, LAPE-initialization, prompt-comparison and cost results; SCULPT scores 50.5 on BeaverTails and 30.6 on GoEmotions. Retained benchmark means are largely unchanged, but APEX's Dis deviation changes from 21.2 to 2.2. Reporting conflicts also appear: LAPE/Misinfo is 43.6 in Table 2 but 35.4 in Table 8, and LAPE-initialized multi-label scores disagree between Tables 2 and 9.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, tree representation and UCB algorithms are retained. Additional equations for critic outputs, nodewise aggregation and actor updates restate operations already described in v1. No new mathematical assumptions, properties, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds prominent claims of effective optimization without human-written initial prompts, information preservation demonstrated through three metrics, and 50% lower computational cost than ProTeGi. Its contribution statement also expands to multi-label tasks. These materially broaden the retained claims about hierarchical refinement, performance and perturbation robustness.

C2.justification: v2 links ProTeGi's performance failures to information loss and excessive prompt changes, interprets automated initialization as an alternative to expert prompts, and attributes cost savings to fewer calls and tokens. It removes v1's manual-initialization limitation and structuring/co-reference future-work discussion, while retaining the two-model and English-only evaluation boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 supplies structuring and comparative-evaluation templates in Appendices N and O, initial prompts for the two new tasks, and the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model identifier with overlapping-chunk handling. Existing critic, actor, rephrasing and search specifications largely carry over. No new code or data release is documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GoEmotions, BeaverTails and Sentence-BERT, while removing Juneja et al.'s task-facet work, the BIG-BENCH reference and OpenAI's 2023 prompting guide. Existing prompt-optimization coverage largely remains, with positioning revised to emphasize information loss from regenerating whole prompts.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Aggregation becomes a separate subsection, results gain new analytical subsections, and appendix organization changes. Terminology is revised throughout, including Preliminary Assessment to Structural Reflection and Long-APE to LAPE.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the main GPT-4o uncertainty table with a ten-task mean-only display and separate appendix tables. It adds three radar plots and a cost table, and moves the prompt-edit illustration and prompt-length table into the appendix. Most existing diagrams and action-distribution plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The initialization experiment addresses a limitation explicitly deferred in v1, while multi-label tests and new templates strengthen applicability evidence and reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement. Conflicting values across v2 Tables 2, 8 and 9, unsupported claims of consistent superiority for LAPE-initialized SCULPT, and generalizing the cost finding from one Formal Fallacy comparison weaken the additions.
